Hi —

Appreciate the questions. Short answers below and I’ve linked the evidence bundle in Drive (shared read-only): https://drive.redwood.com/shared/evidence/horizon-2026-subproc-bundle

- KMS providers: we use a combination depending on deployment mode. Hosted API customers are under Redwood-managed keys (AWS KMS in us-west-2, GCP KMS in europe-west1 for EU-region tenants). Dedicated/Private customers may bring their own KMS (BYOK) or configure a dedicated key in their cloud account.
- Key custody: hosted keys are managed by Redwood (we do not export private key material). For BYOK customers, the customer retains control; we only receive wrapped keys as necessary for provisioning.
- Rotation: hosted KMS keys are rotated annually for root CMKs; data encryption keys are rotated per best practice (90-180 days depending on workload). We can provide the SOC2 section that maps to key management controls — see soc2_type2_summary_2025.pdf (page references included in the Drive bundle).
- Subprocessor wrap/unwrap: no downstream subprocessor has persistent wrap/unwrap privileges for customer key material. Ephemeral wrapping for provisioning occurs via ephemeral HSM sessions in our dedicated onboarding flows and is logged (audit IDs included in the bundle).

Action: I’ve uploaded the annotated roster (row-level residency, TTLs, access types) and a short README explaining where to find the SOC2 notes and HSM attestations. Willing to hop on a 30-min call if your reviewers want to walk through the artifacts tomorrow.

Connor O
